item.title: The Royal Navy Is Retiring Yet Another Frigate—and Has Nothing to Replace It
item.description: The Royal Navy recently invested in significant upgrades to the HMS Richmond—even with the knowledge that it would be decommissioned well before 2030. The post The Royal Navy Is Retiring Yet Another Frigate—and Has Nothing to Replace It appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Another US Air Force Base in Japan Is Getting the F-35 Soon
item.description: The US Air Force is expected to station F-35 fighter jets at Misawa Air Base, a major base in northern Honshu. The post Another US Air Force Base in Japan Is Getting the F-35 Soon appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Who’s Afraid of Russia’s Sixth-Generation Warplanes? (No One)
item.description: Russia’s war economy is fully devoted to the struggle in Ukraine—giving the Kremlin few resources for long-term projects like a sixth-gen fighter jet. The post Who’s Afraid of Russia’s Sixth-Generation Warplanes? (No One) appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Tobol: Understanding Russia’s Great Baltic Satellite Jammer
item.description: A crucial part of anti-satellite warfare is thwarting the GPS navigation systems that modern “smart” weapons systems rely on—and Russia’s Tobol system may have cracked this code. The post Tobol: Understanding Russia’s Great Baltic Satellite Jammer appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Pakistan’s JF-17 Thunder: The $30 Million Fighter Jet Rewriting the Arms Market
item.description: Pakistan’s JF-17 appears to be roughly as effective as Western fighter jets—at a third of the upfront price tag, and with far lower ongoing costs. The post Pakistan’s JF-17 Thunder: The $30 Million Fighter Jet Rewriting the Arms Market appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Missile Reality Check: Why War with Iran Could Break Israel’s Missile Shield
item.description: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu estimated that Israel could absorb more than 700 missile strikes from Iran. But Iran has far more than 700 missiles in its stockpiles… The post The Missile Reality Check: Why War with Iran Could Break Israel’s Missile Shield appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Russia’s Mediterranean Fleet Is Returning Home—and the UK Is Watching
item.description: Russia is increasingly escorting its “ghost fleet” vessels with naval assets—helping to protect them from Western seizure, but making their affiliation with the Kremlin far more obvious. The post Russia’s Mediterranean Fleet Is Returning Home—and the UK Is Watching appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: US Military “Ready, Willing, and Able” to Bomb Iran, Trump Says
item.description: President Donald Trump took to social media on Wednesday to warn Iran of impending military strikes if its leaders did not seek a wide-ranging political settlement. The post US Military “Ready, Willing, and Able” to Bomb Iran, Trump Says appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Donald Trump Should Visit Central Asia in 2026
item.description: While the White House has paid more attention to Central Asia than past administrations, it is unclear where the region fits on the US priority list. The post Why Donald Trump Should Visit Central Asia in 2026 appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Iraq’s Next Government Won’t Shake off Iran’s Influence
